log.text: Floette used Light of Ruin → Basculegion
Light Screen up on P2's side
Floette used Light of Ruin → Grimmsnarl

decisions.rationale: Mega Floette is the intended Mega. Floette-Dedenne lead immediately pressures Pelipper and Basculegion with Energy Ball, Thunderbolt, Nuzzle, and Protect while retaining strong Light of Ruin damage. Milotic and Mamoswine complete the plan: Milotic supplies Icy Wind, Competitive, and rain stability; Mamoswine pressures Hisuian Arcanine and Garganacl with High Horsepower.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette remains the primary win condition. Against rain, prioritize preserving Floette while using Dedenne and Milotic to disrupt Pelipper/Basculegion speed and damage. Mamoswine is the preferred backline answer to Hisuian Arcanine and Garganacl; avoid exposing it unnecessarily to Water attacks.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: none. Lead Pelipper+Basculegion: set rain and Adaptability Water STAB turn 1. Grimmsnarl+Garganacl complete plan with screens, Prankster control, and physical walling vs opponent Fairy/Steel/Dark cores.
decisions.notebook: Rain core punishes Talonflame/Mamoswine; double Prankster handles speed control and priority; Garganacl walls physical; Hisuian Arcanine for Intimidate pivots. Covers Fairy/Steel/Dark and speed demons.

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 2 (Basculegion) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Mega Light of Ruin and Magnet Thunderbolt pressure both active foes for potential double KOs, removing rain’s offensive core before Tailwind matters. Dedenne moves first and Thunderbolt targets Pelipper’s 4x weakness; Mega Floette targets Basculegion directly. This preserves the primary win condition while avoiding unnecessary exposure.
Tailwind secures speed control next turn; both Protect to safely scout fast Electric/Fairy offense in rain.
Grimmsnarl Prankster gives immediate speed control and Parting Shot vs fast Fairy/Electric core pressuring Basculegion; Garganacl too slow here.
decisions.notebook: Rain punishes Talonflame/Mamoswine; double Prankster for speed/screens/priority; Garganacl physical wall; plan Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate pivot vs Fairy/Steel/Dark and speed demons.

decisions.rationale: Floette moves before Grimmsnarl and can remove it with Light of Ruin, though accuracy is imperfect. Dedenne moves before Basculegion and uses accurate single-target Thunderbolt to pressure the immediate Water threat without spread reduction. This preserves the Mega win condition while denying screens and reducing Basculegion's ability to attack freely.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette remains the primary win condition. Against rain, prioritize preserving Floette while using Dedenne and Milotic to disrupt opposing speed and damage. Mamoswine is the preferred backline answer to Hisuian Arcanine and Garganacl; avoid exposing it unnecessarily to Water attacks. Opponent has shown early Protect usage from Basculegion; account for Protect when planning doubles targeting.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Basculegion)
Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Prankster Light Screen lands first vs faster special attackers; Basculegion Protect scouts while reduced rate still viable; sets up for Garganacl pivot and remaining Prankster turns.
decisions.notebook: Double Prankster screens priority core; Garganacl physical wall vs physical; Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate pivot planned vs Fairy/Steel/Dark and speed control; Rain punishes Talonflame/Mamoswine.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Protect preserves Floette from Basculegion’s priority while Dedenne’s Thunderbolt removes Basculegion from 46%. Garganacl gets one action, but cannot immediately threaten Floette through Protect; this preserves the Mega win condition and leaves Energy Ball to finish Garganacl next turn.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion has shown repeated early Protect usage. Opponent’s rain mode relies heavily on Water pressure and priority; preserve Mega Floette while using Dedenne and Milotic to disrupt speed and damage. Mamoswine remains the preferred backline answer to Garganacl and Hisuian Arcanine.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Basculegion)
decisions.rationale: Foes faster and SE on Basculegion; Wide Guard + Protect scouts, preserves Light Screen, and avoids free KO while Rain persists.
decisions.notebook: Double Prankster screens core; Garganacl physical wall; planned Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate pivot vs Fairy/Steel/Dark + speed control; Rain punishes Talonflame/Mamoswine.

decisions.rationale: Energy Ball is the strongest single-target answer to Garganacl and bypasses Wide Guard. Thunderbolt acts before Basculegion and is calculated to KO from 46%; this also punishes another Protect attempt. Floette remains vulnerable but can remove Garganacl before it acts.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion has repeatedly used Protect early, including after taking substantial damage; punish this with simultaneous single-target pressure rather than relying on spread attacks. Opponent’s rain mode depends on Water pressure and priority. Preserve Mega Floette when practical; Mamoswine remains the preferred backline answer to Garganacl and Hisuian Arcanine.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine is the preferred answer to Garganacl and takes neutral Rock Slide while threatening it next turn with super-effective High Horsepower. Milotic is safer immediately but gives Garganacl more room to Recover or Salt Cure; preserve Mamoswine for this matchup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent repeatedly Protects early with Basculegion, so use simultaneous single-target pressure rather than spread attacks when it returns in future games. Their rain mode relies on Water pressure and priority. Preserve Mega Floette when practical; Mamoswine is the preferred backline answer to Garganacl and Hisuian Arcanine.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Basculegion)
decisions.rationale: Wide Guard blocks Electroweb/spreads; Aqua Jet +1 prio KOs 37% Floette before it acts; Basc survives next hit at 46% with screens up.

High Horsepower is super-effective and calculated to OHKO Garganacl, while Thunderbolt adds insurance against a miss and pressures Recover. Nuzzle cannot affect Purifying Salt, and spread attacks are unnecessary. Single-target moves bypass Wide Guard.
decisions.notebook: Opponent repeatedly Protects early with Basculegion; use simultaneous single-target pressure rather than spread attacks when it returns. Their rain mode relies on Water pressure and priority. Preserve Mega Floette when practical; Mamoswine is the preferred backline answer to Garganacl and Hisuian Arcanine.

decisions.rationale: Garganacl at full HP; Salt Cure pressures Mamoswine (main physical threat) while Rain and Light Screen remain; Wide Guard unnecessary vs mostly single-target; Rock Slide risks miss and no KO.

reflections.summary: Won because Dedenne’s immediate Electric pressure removed Pelipper and then heavily damaged Basculegion, while Mega Floette punished Grimmsnarl and forced the opponent’s defensive Protect/Wide Guard pattern. The four brought and Mega Floette were well suited to this rain-and-screen mode, though Floette was exposed to Aqua Jet.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Mega Floette as the intended Mega, but plan to preserve it through Basculegion’s priority range: use Protect or switch after its initial pressure instead of leaving it vulnerable. Continue pairing focused Electric pressure with Mamoswine’s Ground coverage rather than relying on spread attacks into Wide Guard.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s rain mode combines Pelipper’s Drizzle with strong Water pressure and Basculegion priority; Basculegion frequently Protects early. Grimmsnarl uses Prankster Light Screen, while Garganacl repeatedly uses Wide Guard to punish spread attacks. Focused single-target pressure is effective. Mega Floette is an excellent offensive answer to their rain/screen core but must be preserved from Aqua Jet. Mamoswine is a strong backline answer to Garganacl and Hisuian Arcanine; retain it when those threats are plausible. Future plan: lead or position Dedenne for immediate Electric pressure, preserve Floette against priority, and avoid defaulting to spread moves into Garganacl.

reflections.summary: Lost because team-preview brought Grimmsnarl screens + Pelipper rain into Dedenne + Mega Floette; electric spam and Fairy Aura removed the core before Garganacl could wall.
reflections.adjustment: Next game drop Grimmsnarl from the four; bring Hisuian Arcanine pivot instead to handle Fairy/electric pressure and contest speed control.
reflections.notebook: Opponent leads Dedenne+ Floette-Mega and spams Magnet Thunderbolt; Rain does not reliably punish Mamoswine; planned Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate pivot vs Fairy/Steel/Dark + speed control; Double Prankster screens core; Garganacl physical wall.
